text:
Alyssa: heads up — production perf regression after last week's FA-variant bump. 95p latency for text-gen rose ~18% on 8k seq workloads. Noticed this after a canary push to dedicated.
Kevin: ugh. which repo/tag? FA main or the patched fork we pulled? any repro script?
Alyssa: flash-attn@v1.1.4 -> v1.2.0 (we pulled upstream change that changed chunking heuristics). repro script: ./bench/run_textgen.sh --model=gpt-j --seq=8192 --batch=4 --iters=50
Alyssa: baseline (v1.1.4): 95p=210ms, tokens/s=5200. after bump: 95p=248ms, tokens/s=4400. CPU debounce small, GPU SM utilization dropped ~6%.
Maria: pushed a quick profile from the canary: flamegraph shows more time in CUDA kernel launch overhead and a new memcpy path inside flash_attn_mixed.cu. link: https://internal.perf/redwood/fg/1785009123
Maria: here's the perf command I ran locally to capture NVTX and traces:

```
nvprof --unified-memory-profiling off --log-file nvlog.txt python -u benchmarks/throughput.py --model bloom-3b --seq-len 8192 --batch 2
nvprof2flame nvlog.txt > bloom-3b-8192.svg
```

Maria: nvprof indicates increased # of kernel launches for the same attention op (paging behavior changed). also see larger kv-cache buffer churn for small prompt prefixes.
Devon: could be the chunking tweak in FA that enables paged-attention fallback for >4k; we enabled a new path that shards q/k/v into pages. vendor note: "paged fallback enables OOM safety but costs launch overhead". pinging upstream PR 3892.
Kevin: we also pulled xformers@v0.2.18 which has optimized fused kernels — might be some ABI mismatch causing suboptimal kernel selection. can you run the small bisect? try disabling xformers to see if FA alone is culprit.
Alyssa: good call. I ran two quick experiments:
- With xformers disabled, flash-attn v1.2.0 still regresses but slightly less: 95p=236ms
- With flash-attn pinned to v1.1.4 and xformers v0.2.18: 95p=212ms (so xformers alone isn't the main regression)
CI-bot: nightly-regression: job/attn-bench-8192 failed threshold check — alerted @eng-runtime on PagerDuty
Kevin: next steps: 1) bisect FA commits between v1.1.4..v1.2.0 for chunking changes; 2) run microbench per-kernel to confirm launch vs compute time; 3) try config knob: FA_PAGED_THRESHOLD=6144 to force old path and measure.
Maria: I exported per-kernel timings from CUPTI. diff shows new kernel flash_attn_forward_paged with many small launches. compute time per launch is tiny but launch overhead dominates at these seq lengths. attaching snippet:

```
flash_attn_forward (old): calls=1, time=180ms
flash_attn_forward_paged (new): calls=12, time=220ms (launch overhead ~3.3ms each)
```

Maria: also KV cache churn: when page size != kv allocation stride our memcopy path hits the fallback memmove which is synchronous.
Devon: for batching heuristics, maybe we can adjust our continuous-batching window so pages align across requests — reduces extra memcpy. config candidates: batch_align_pages=true, page_size=1024
Alyssa: I mocked batch_align_pages=true in dev and saw tokens/s +8% (95p down to 228ms). promising but not a full fix.
Kevin: let's open two issues upstream: (A) FA: reduce kernel launches or merge small launches; (B) xformers: ensure kernel selection doesn't pick paged path for steady-state long sequences. include traces and CUPTI outputs.
Alyssa: I drafted PR descriptions and reproduction steps. also adding a temporary runtime flag to force legacy non-paged path for customers who opt-in.
Devon: vendor drop note — one vendor vendorX wants to remove their fused-attn shim next quarter. if they drop it we lose a fallback path. we should test falling back to our fused kernels before that happens.
Maria: added perf runs matrix to the ticket: models=[bloom-3b,gpt-j], seq=[2048,4096,8192], batch=[1,2,4], kernels=[flash-attn v1.1.4,v1.2.0,xformers v0.2.17, v0.2.18]
Kevin: thanks. assign owners? Alyssa -> reproduce + runtime flag. Maria -> CUPTI traces + issue attachments. Devon -> vendor compatibility + batch heuristic experiment. I'll triage upstream PRs.
Alyssa: TL;DR action items in thread: bisect FA, flip batch_align_pages flag A/B test, open upstream issues with traces, temporary runtime opt-out flag, measure impact across matrices.
Devon: I'll also add an alert rule for sudden 95p regressions when kernel-launch count increases >20%.
Alyssa: sweet. I'll update the canary roadmap and schedule a rollback window if no fix by next deploy. :thumbsup:
CI-bot: created ticket INFR-4912 (attn-kernel-upstream-regression) and linked perf artifacts.
Kevin: ok. I'll post a short summary to eng-runtime weekly notes.
